title: Basic Commands [ls -a]
description:
# ls -a
---
`ls` shows files in a directory. But it hides files that start with a dot (`.`). These are called **hidden files**.

`ls -a` shows ALL files, including hidden ones.

Why does this matter? Some files are hidden for a reason... and some are hidden to HIDE things.

---
